name: Karley Solorzano
why: A sharp, evenly lit, front-facing frame of her accepting an SGA award, cropped to her alone. The best photograph of any of this block available.
caption_quote: Karley Soloranzo receives Chief Justice’s Verdict Award from Isaac King on Wednesday, Oct. 18.
id_note: Two people, both named. The certificate she is holding is legible in the frame and reads Chief Justice’s Verdict Award, September 2023, Karley Solorzano, so the recipient is identified by the document in her own hands. The man beside her is Chief Justice Isaac King: the archive’s existing 2023-24-isaac-king.jpg is cut from this same photograph. The Herald caption misspells her surname Soloranzo; the certificate and SGA’s own legislation both give Solorzano.

name: Maggie Phelps
why: A studio portrait, single subject, sharp and evenly lit. The best photograph of anyone in this block.
caption_quote: Maggie Phelps is a member of the news staff for the Herald for Fall 2023.
id_note: Single-subject captioned mug, so the name is unambiguous. Proved to be the SGA Maggie Phelps by matching it against the Herald frame of 28 April 2026 captioned 'New Judicial Council member Maggie Phelps speaks with fellow judicial council members' (042826_sga_KH06.jpg): the left-hand woman there has the same fair strawberry-blonde hair, the same pale blue eyes, the same fine sparse brows and the same small gold ring in the right nostril. A previous pass set this mug aside on the ground that it ties her to the newspaper rather than to SGA; the objection was relevance, not identity, and the 2026 SGA frame closes the identity question. The 042826 frame itself stays withdrawn and is not the file offered here.

name: Matthew Winiger
why: The archive records this person twice under two spellings of the surname, so the portrait reached only one of the two and the other read as somebody nobody had found. Same photograph, the WKU News portrait of him as president-elect.
caption_quote: (the same photograph as the other spelling)
id_note: Spelling variant, flagged rather than fixed. The archive's own 2020-21 note on Matthew Winiger reads 'The minutes spell the surname both Winiger and Wininger; unsettled which is correct.' The 2020-21 Winiger chaired the Sustainability Committee from October 2020 to March 2021; the 2021-22 president Matthew Wininger ran on continuing the recycling and sustainability work, and Zachary Skillman's record says he continued the initiatives Wininger had started. One man, one office followed by another. If an editor judges them two people, drop this entry; the 2021-22 portrait is unaffected.

name: Molly Ricky
why: The archive records this person twice under two spellings of the surname, so the portrait reached only one of the two and the other read as somebody nobody had found. Same photograph, the Herald frame of her being sworn in.
caption_quote: Molly Ricke is sworn into as a Senator-at-Large
id_note: Spelling variant, flagged rather than fixed. Molly Ricke sat as a senator from January 2025 and authored spring 2026 legislation (Bill 19-26-S); 'Molly Ricky' exists in the archive on the strength of one Herald sentence about the 26th Senate's first meeting on 28 April 2026, where a sitting senator of that name ran for Speaker. Two senators whose names differ by one letter sitting in the same chamber in the same month is not credible, and no second Molly Rick- appears anywhere in SGA's minutes or legislation. The Herald's own frame of the speaker vote that day shows three women at the lectern, the leftmost of whom matches the sworn-in portrait on hairline, freckling, nose and jaw, but that frame carries no caption naming her and is not relied on. If an editor judges them two people, drop this entry; the 2025-26 portrait is unaffected.

name: Emaun Riley
why: A sharp, well-lit, front-facing frame of him walking off the stage after winning an award, cropped to him alone. The best photograph of anyone in this block.
caption_quote: Emaun Riley of Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity Inc. goes in for a hug with a family member
id_note: The caption names one person; the only other figure is the unnamed family member, who has her back to the camera. Riley is therefore the man facing the camera, and his face fills the frame. The caption's description of him is confirmed inside the photograph: his necktie is printed with the Phi Beta Sigma letters and the founding year 1914. Emaun Riley is a distinctive name and no second student of it appears anywhere in the Herald library.

name: Evan Tuck
why: A sharp, evenly lit, front-facing frame of him carrying his fraternity's award off the stage, cropped to him alone.
caption_quote: Sigma Phi Epsilon chapter president Evan Tuck carries the M. Reed Morgan Fraternal Excellence Award
id_note: One named subject. The identification is fixed by the object in his hands rather than by position: the trophy he is carrying is legible in the frame and reads M. REED MORGAN FRATERNAL EXCELLENCE AWARD, and the plaque in his other hand carries the WKU mark and the same award name, which is exactly what the caption says he is carrying. The two other people in the wider frame are a woman standing on the stage behind him and a man in a navy suit leaving the lectern, neither of them holding an award. Confirmed to be the SGA Evan Tuck from the Herald's own report of the April 2025 election, which lists Evan Tuck among the Senators at Large elected for 2025-26 (wkuherald.com/83881); the Greek Week Convocation falls inside that same academic year.

name: Jakob Briggs
why: The only Herald frame that names him. A sharp, well-lit three-quarter view of his face, cropped to him alone out of a crowd scene.
caption_quote: Jakob Briggs, a member of Phi Beta Sigma Fraternity, Inc., participates in the Walk for Suicide Prevention
id_note: One named subject. He is the only person in the frame in sharp focus, everyone in the foreground being thrown out by the shallow depth of field, and the only person identifiable as what the caption calls him: his sweatshirt is legible in the crop and reads PROPERTY OF PHI BETA SIGMA, 1914, ATHLETIC DEPARTMENT. A second Black man stands behind him in the frame, out of focus and half hidden, wearing no fraternity letters; he is cropped out. The spelling Jakob Briggs is distinctive and no second student of that name appears in the Herald library. The frame is dated March 2025, two years after his 2022-23 Senate term, but nothing in it is personal to him: he is walking with his fraternity at a public campus awareness event, and the caption attributes no statement or circumstance to him.

name: Jacob Skillman
why: The only Herald photograph that names him. A cross-country practice frame, cropped to him alone; the face is a small three-quarter view mid-stride but it is sharp and lit, and nothing else exists.
caption_quote: (left) sophomore Anthony Sweet and (right) sophomore Jacob Skillman practicing
id_note: Two runners in the frame and the Herald's own record for the photograph positions them, Sweet left and Skillman right, so the right-hand runner in the long-sleeved shirt is Skillman. That positional wording is carried in the Herald's stored caption for the image, not in the shorter caption printed under it in the article, and it is also the slug of the Herald's own attachment URL for the file. Proved to be the SGA Jacob Skillman from the Herald's own reporting rather than from the name alone: its C-USA academic honours lists of 7 and 8 May 2020 put both Jacob Skillman and Zach Skillman on WKU men's cross country, its report of 15 September 2021 names Jacob Skillman among the senate members sworn in that night, and its profile of 23 September 2021 calls Senator Jacob Skillman a junior, which makes him a sophomore in October 2020 exactly as this caption does.
